name: Capture - Quick Notes
subcategory: quick capture inbox for Apple devices
tagline: Catch notes, links, images, and files now, then send them to the app where they belong

pricing.notes: The US App Store also lists a $9.99 yearly subscription. Regional prices vary.

verdictSummary: Capture's full core loop uses public Apple frameworks and documented integration points. A coding agent can create native apps for Apple's platforms, sync the shared inbox through iCloud, add widgets and system capture actions, and route items through destination-specific logic for more than 40 third-party apps. The integration catalog is the largest part, but it does not depend on a proprietary network or dataset.
coreLoopDIY: Catch text, links, images, and files from any Apple device, sync them through iCloud, organize them into lists, then send each item to more than 40 third-party apps through destination-specific export logic.
requirements: Apple Developer account for iCloud and App Group entitlements
whatYouLose: App Store-ready polish across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro
years of CloudKit migration, conflict, and offline-sync edge cases
ongoing maintenance for more than 40 destination-specific export integrations
the localization, accessibility, and device test matrix
fast compatibility updates when Apple or a destination app changes behavior
moatNotes: maintenance across Apple platforms, CloudKit, system integrations, and more than 40 destination-specific exporters
whyPeopleStillPay: People buy Capture to avoid maintaining the same workflow across Apple's platforms. The one-time purchase includes iCloud sync, deep system integration, and more than 40 third-party export destinations whose URL schemes, APIs, Shortcuts, and content rules can change independently.

prompt:
Build me a native quick-capture inbox across Apple platforms to replace Capture. Requirements:

- Use Swift 6, SwiftUI, SwiftData, CloudKit, App Intents, WidgetKit, and AppKit where
  macOS needs it. Create one Xcode project with a shared Swift package.
- Target iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Give each platform a
  native layout while sharing the model, persistence, search, and export engine.
- A capture stores text, detected URLs, phone numbers, reminder dates, images, files,
  its list, archive state, and created and edited dates. Use NSDataDetector.
- Store locally first with SwiftData and sync through the user's private CloudKit
  database. Support offline writes, retries, conflict merging, and schema migration.
- Provide Inbox, Archive, lists, full-text search, quick editing, undoable archive and
  restore, safe deletion, JSON import and export, and automatic local backups.
- Add a share extension for text, URLs, images, and files; configurable widgets for
  quick capture, lists, and single items; Siri and Shortcuts actions through App Intents.
- On Mac, add a menu bar app, global quick-capture shortcut, compact floating window,
  and keyboard navigation. On Watch, support fast text and voice capture.
- Build a catalog of at least 40 concrete export adapters. Each adapter owns supported
  content types, validation, settings, encoding, and its destination-specific behavior.
- Support URL and x-callback-url schemes, EventKit, Photos, Mail, bundled Shortcuts, and
  REST APIs. Store API credentials in Keychain and report export failures without data loss.
- No Capture account, telemetry, ads, or proprietary backend. Network access is limited
  to private iCloud sync and exports the user explicitly triggers.
- Out of scope: billing and analytics. Do not omit an Apple target or replace the 40-plus
  adapter catalog with a generic share sheet.
- Test CloudKit conflict handling, extensions, widgets, content detection, backups, and
  every export adapter. Document entitlements, App Groups, iCloud, keys, and setup.
